messages:
eval-bot: nightly-eval alert for redwood-v7.2: promptset 'csv_parsing_checks' fail rate jumped to 15% (baseline 0.6%). Affected only structured-output prompts with fenced code blocks. Full report: https://ci.internal/reports/4109876543

maria (ml-eng): saw the alert. repro locally yet? which exact checkpoint + tokenizer?

eval-bot: checkpoint: redwood-v7.2-weight-mix-2026-03-19, tokenizer: mergeset-2026-03-18 (PR #4821 applied). Repro script below.

cheng (research): quick repro + tiny diff: mergeset change split U+0060 handling so triple-backtick fences now tokenized as separate tokens rather than single fence token. That produces extra newline tokens inside code fences -> downstream CSV parser thinks a row break. failing prompt ids: 42, 87, 129 from csv_parsing_checks.

maria (ml-eng): can you paste one failing example (input and model output)?

cheng (research): here — reproduced with the eval script:
```jsonl
{"id":42,"prompt":"Name,Description
\"foo\",\"Example: ```python
print(1)
```\"\n","model":"redwood-v7.2"}
```
model output (truncated):
```text
Name,Description
\"foo\",\"Example: ```python
print(1)
```\"
\n
\"bar\",\"Broken row starts here because tokenizer injected \n inside fence\"
```
The extra \n inside the code fence is coming from new token boundary behavior.

olivia (platform): hmm. Is quantization involved here? did we change any kernel that could scramble tokens?

sam (oncall): logs show failures across fp16 and int8 canaries — looks model-agnostic. Tokenization stage is before quant paths so likely tokenizer.

cheng (research): confirmed: repro on fp16 and int8. Running `python eval/run_promptset.py --model redwood-v7.2 --promptset tests/csv_parsing_checks --save out.jsonl` reproduces the split. Quick diff of mergeset: `- "`\u0060" : 1001 => + "`": 1001, "`": 1002` (mergeset reordering introduced a separate token for backtick sequence).

maria (ml-eng): proposed mitigation: revert tokenizer mergeset change for U+0060, stage a canary build pinned to previous mergeset, and re-run the full csv_parsing_checks. If revert is heavy, we can add a preprocessing step that normalizes triple-backticks to a single sentinel token before tokenization. Thoughts?

olivia (platform): I can spin a canary with old mergeset and deploy to dedicated-canary-01. ETA ~25m. Which commit to revert?

sam (oncall): target revert commit: 3a9f2b7 (the mergeset update). If rollback needed, I can coordinate the revert and hotfix rollout.

cheng (research): small repro command for token-trace: `DEBUG_TOKEN_TRACE=1 python eval/run_promptset.py --model redwood-v7.2 --promptset tests/csv_parsing_checks --ids 42,87 --out debug_trace.json` — this emits token boundaries that show the extra \n token inside fence.

eval-bot: acknowledged — I'll run the traces and post token-level diffs once canary is up.

maria (ml-eng): follow-up actions: 1) olivia to deploy canary with old mergeset to dedicated-canary-01 (in 25m). 2) cheng to add unit test for fenced code -> CSV integrity to nightly eval suite. 3) sam to prepare revert PR (3a9f2b7 revert) ready if canary confirms. 4) eval-bot to post pass rate update.

olivia (platform): canary request submitted. capacity ETA 25m, will post link to canary runs.

maria (ml-eng): thanks — please add a regression note to onboarding docs that mergeset changes to punctuation must include fenced-code integration test.

cheng (research): noted. I'll add the unit test and a short reproducer script in tests/repro/4109876543_repro.sh.

sam (oncall): if we need an emergency rollback, target window is next 2 hours; alert paging will be used.

maria (ml-eng): good catch everyone. tagging this as triage-in-progress. Will follow up in thread when canary results are in. :thumbsup:
